findings.evidence: Lock pairing is authorized from tracked filenames/counts rather than from a successfully parsed supported direct manifest. NuGet accepts packages.lock.json when CountTrackedNuGetProjects reports exactly one same-root .csproj, and npm accepts a lock whenever a same-root package.json is tracked. Direct manifests are parsed independently and may be malformed, unsupported, conditional, or yield no supported fact, yet the matching lock can still emit Medium-confidence framework evidence. The correction tests cover no manifest, a valid unique manifest, and multiple same-root project files, but do not cover a single invalid/unsupported direct manifest plus a matching lock.
findings.correction_outcome: Track successfully validated supported direct-manifest identities and roots, and allow lock-derived facts only when exactly one valid supported owner at the same root is established. Add RED tests for malformed, unsupported, and conditional single-manifest-plus-lock cases for both NuGet and npm; require bounded audit diagnostics and no lock-derived fact, while retaining the valid unique-owner cases.
